citation: Donnellan, M. B., Oswald, F. L., Baird, B. M., & Lucas, R. E. (2006). The Mini-IPIP scales: Tiny-yet-effective measures of the Big Five factors of personality. Psychological Assessment, 18, 192-203.
license: Mini-IPIP items are public domain (IPIP); third-person rewording is permitted. Observer items are original (Lane).
why_included: Meta-analyses show ratings by people who know you predict job and academic performance better than self-reports, and add to them (Connelly & Ones, 2010; Oh, Wang & Mount, 2011). This is the single biggest accuracy upgrade available that most competitors skip.

flow.invite: After the personality session, the user invites 3-5 people who know them well from different contexts (family, friend, teammate/colleague). Each rater gets a link; no account needed.
flow.minimum: Aggregate only when >= 2 raters have completed. Report self vs others side by side, never a single blended score.
flow.privacy: Individual rater answers are never shown to the user; only the aggregate of 2+ raters. Tell raters this before they start.

response_format.stem: How accurately does each statement describe {name}, compared with other people of the same sex and roughly the same age?

scoring.domain: Mean of 4 items per domain. Aggregate across raters by mean, weighting raters who report knowing the person 'well' or 'very well' x1.5.
